questions.q: On a bank statement, how does a Payables disbursement typically appear?
options: As a debit, often with a check number or EFT trace number
As a credit with a lockbox code
It never appears on the bank statement
As a zero-amount transaction
questions.explain: A Payables payment is an outflow, appearing as a debit on the statement, typically matched by amount and a reference like a check or trace number.

questions.q: What should happen when a check is voided before it ever clears the bank?
options: It should still appear as a statement debit that gets manually matched
Receivables must reverse the original receipt
There is no real-world bank event, so the system transaction should get no matching statement line
It automatically becomes a lockbox deposit
questions.explain: If a check is voided before clearing, nothing happened at the bank, so there's nothing to reconcile against.

questions.q: What is a lockbox deposit, in the context of reconciling Receivables receipts?
options: A single customer's payment split across multiple bank accounts
A bank batching several customers' payments into one deposit line, often requiring a one-to-many match
A payment that can never be reconciled
A type of Payables disbursement
questions.explain: A lockbox deposit lumps multiple customer payments into a single statement line, which is exactly the one-to-many match type scenario.

questions.q: What does a 'reversed receipt,' such as an NSF returned check, look like on the bank statement?
options: A credit matching the original receipt exactly
A duplicate of the original deposit
It never shows up on the statement at all
A debit that offsets a credit that was already reconciled
questions.explain: An NSF or reversed receipt shows up as an offsetting debit, and needs to be traced back to the original receipt so Receivables can reverse it.

questions.q: In the worked example, why did Thornbury Retail Group's payment need Treasury's attention?
options: Because the EFT trace number was missing from the statement
Because Kestrel Supply Co. disputed the invoice
Because the payment bounced for insufficient funds and had to be traced back to the original receipt
Because the payment was a lockbox deposit
questions.explain: The customer's payment was reversed (NSF) days later, requiring it to be traced back to the original receipt so Receivables could reverse it.
